description: English closed-class (function) words, by Universal Dependencies part of speech. A closed class is finite by definition, so it is declared here rather than learned; WordNet holds none of these words. A word may belong to several classes: 'to' is a preposition and the infinitive marker, 'that' a determiner, pronoun and conjunction. 'features' marks UD morphological features: PronType=Tot is UD's total (collective) quantifier -- 'all', 'every', 'each', 'everything' -- which applies what is said to every member of what it quantifies. PronType=Prs marks the personal pronouns and PronType=Dem the demonstratives; Person, Gender and Reflex=Yes (the reflexives) are declared for the personal pronouns, as the UD English Web Treebank annotates them. Definite=Def marks the definite article 'the' and Definite=Ind the indefinite articles 'a' and 'an', as the treebank annotates them: a noun phrase that 'the' opens names one thing, so 'the capital of France' and 'Paris' can name the same thing, while 'a city' names any of several. A word takes one value of a feature: 'that', a demonstrative and a relative pronoun, is declared PronType=Dem, although the treebank's train split annotates the pronoun 'that' PronType=Rel 556 times and PronType=Dem 295 times. 'capitalized' lists the closed-class words written with a capital wherever they stand in a sentence, not only at its start: in the UD English Web Treebank r2.18 (train, dev and test), 'i' is the only closed-class word written capitalized in most of its occurrences after a sentence's first word (2090 of 2413). Loaded by Brain.Lexicon.ClosedClass.
